jobs.title: Algorithm Engineer, Deep Learning
jobs.description:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.

  
  
  

**Group/Division**

The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The Broadband Plasma (BBP) division is the market-leading optical inspection system used by logic, foundry, and memory customers to detect critical defects at advanced nodes. These tools combine broadband plasma technology with unmatched sensitivity and speed to support high-volume manufacturing.

**What You'll Do**

In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.

  
  

We are looking for a full-time **Deep Learning, Algorithm Engineer** who is passionate about pioneering **Deep Learning (DL)** , **foundation models** , and **GenAI** for the defect detection/classification applications in the **semiconductor process control** business.

  
  

Qualified candidates are expected to have a strong background and in-depth experience in deep learning, especially in object detection, segmentation, vision foundation models, and multimodal models. Candidates have strong experience in **integrating/grounding DL/GenAI into complex hardware/software systems.**

  

The ideal candidate can work independently across the full deep learning project lifecycle, including conceptualizing, exploring, designing, implementing, and deploying. Responsibilities for this position include, but are not limited to:

* Understand state-of-the-art (SOTA) deep learning and GenAI models.
* Connect SOTA DL modeling approaches to domain problem statements.
* Analyze modeling requirements based on product feature requirements.
* Design deep learning and GenAI models to meet modeling requirements.
* Implement modeling prototypes and perform analysis.
* Perform model training and/or tuning on domain datasets.
* Evaluate and validate model performance against defined metrics.
* Integrate model into a complex system.
* Analyze model performance in a complex system.
* Design new DL modules or components to improve performance.
* Optimize DL or GenAI model throughput and cost.
* Perform A/B testing between models on real data.
* Work and communicate collaboratively with peers.
* Present ideas, concepts, and results in professional technical settings.
  

  

**Qualifications/Education Desired**

* Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related quantitative fields.

* Academic or industrial experience applying deep learning or GenAI to **real-world** problem(s), with impactful results.

* In-depth experience applying deep learning, Vision Foundation Models (VFM), or Vision Language Models (VLM) in at least one of the following areas: computer vision, image processing, robotics, NLP, or equivalent.

* Experience with **GenAI coding tools** for engineering development.

* Proficiency in **Python** and one additional programming language from: C++, Java, Rust.

* Proficiency in at least one deep learning framework (e.g., PyTorch, JAX, or equivalent).

* Demonstrated deep learning or GenAI expertise via **technical publications** in top conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, CVPR, ICML, ICLR, KDD, SIGGRAPH, etc.) and/or **industrial patents** and/or **impactful open-source projects** is required.

* Travel required: up to 10%.

* Experience with DL model optimization for reduced precision (e.g., FP8, FP4) is a plus.

* Experience with VFM pretraining or post-training is a plus.

* Experience in semiconductor process control is a plus.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Doctorate (academic) degree with 0 years of related work experience; or Master’s degree with 3 years of related work experience.

* Academic or industrial experience applying deep learning or GenAI to real-world problem(s), with impactful results.

* Demonstrated deep learning or GenAI expertise via technical publications in top conferences (e.g., NeurIPS, CVPR, ICML, ICLR, KDD, SIGGRAPH, etc.) and/or industrial patents and/or impactful open-source projects is required.

* Travel required: up to 10%.

We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

jobs.description:
Overview:

**ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.**

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.

Responsibilities:

**Role Overview**
=================

We’re looking for a **SLAM Specialist** to design, implement, and advance state-of-the-art simultaneous localization and mapping systems that enable accurate, robust spatial understanding from real-world sensor data. This role is focused on modern SLAM techniques—both classical and learning-based—with an emphasis on scalable state estimation, sensor fusion, and long-term mapping in complex, dynamic environments.

This is a hands-on, research-driven role for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of robotics, computer vision, and probabilistic inference. You’ll collaborate closely with research scientists, ML engineers, and systems teams to translate cutting-edge SLAM ideas into production-ready capabilities that form the backbone of our world modeling stack.

**What You Will Do**
====================

* Design and implement modern SLAM systems for real-world environments, including visual, visual-inertial, lidar, or multi-sensor configurations.
* Develop robust localization and mapping pipelines, including pose estimation, map management, loop closure, and global optimization.
* Research and prototype learning-based or hybrid SLAM approaches that combine classical geometry with modern machine learning methods.
* Build and maintain scalable state estimation frameworks, including factor graph optimization, filtering, and smoothing techniques.
* Develop sensor fusion strategies that integrate cameras, IMUs, depth sensors, lidar, or other modalities to improve robustness and accuracy.
* Analyze failure modes in real-world SLAM deployments (e.g., perceptual aliasing, dynamic scenes, drift) and design principled solutions.
* Create evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and metrics to measure SLAM accuracy, robustness, and performance across large datasets.
* Optimize performance across the stack, including real-time constraints, memory usage, and compute efficiency, for large-scale and production systems.
* Collaborate with reconstruction, simulation, and infrastructure teams to ensure SLAM outputs integrate cleanly with downstream world modeling and rendering pipelines.
* Contribute to technical direction by proposing new research ideas, mentoring teammates, and helping define best practices for localization and mapping across the organization.

**Key Qualifications**
======================

* 6+ years of experience working on SLAM, state estimation, robotics perception, or related areas.
* Strong foundation in probabilistic estimation, optimization, and geometric vision (e.g., bundle adjustment, factor graphs, Kalman filtering).
* Deep experience with one or more SLAM paradigms (visual, visual-inertial, lidar, multi-sensor, or hybrid systems).
* Proficiency in Python and/or C++, with hands-on experience building research or production-grade SLAM systems.
* Experience with numerical optimization libraries and/or robotics frameworks.
* Familiarity with learning-based perception or representation learning and how it can augment classical SLAM pipelines.
* Strong understanding of real-world sensor characteristics, calibration, synchronization, and noise modeling.
* Proven ability to work in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and drive projects from concept through deployment.
* A strong sense of ownership and engineering rigor: you care deeply about correctness, stability, and measurable improvements.
* Enjoy collaborating with a small, high-caliber team and raising the technical bar through thoughtful design, experimentation, and code quality.

**Who You Are**
===============

* **Fearless Innovator:** We need people who thrive on challenges and aren't afraid to tackle the impossible.
* **Resilient Builder:** Impacting Large World Models isn't a sprint; it's a marathon with hurdles. We're looking for builders who can weather the storms of groundbreaking research and come out stronger.
* **Mission-Driven Mindset:** Everything we do is in service of creating the best spatially intelligent AI systems, and using them to empower people.
* **Collaborative Spirit:** We're building something bigger than any one person. We need team players who can harness the power of collective intelligence.

### **Member of Technical Staff, Generalist — Supercompute** **San Francisco, CA · In office, 5 days a week · Full time · 2 openings**

### **About d\_model**

d\_model is an interpretability & alignment AI research lab. We partner with frontier labs to turn their models into capable interpretability and alignment researchers, and we use the agents we build for our own independent research. Our team has worked at OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, EleutherAI and MATS, among other places.

### **About the role**

The Supercompute team builds the systems our researchers depend on every day: sandboxes for AI agents, AI training infrastructure, tools for monitoring AI agents, and the tools that keep a fast-moving research lab coordinated. We're a small team, where every member owns real projects end-to-end.

We're hiring two software engineers who can take full ownership of at least one internal system; from discovering what researchers actually need, through design and build, to running and maintaining it in production. You won't be handed a spec. You'll sit close to our research team, notice where they're slowed down, and decide what to build about it.

This is a generalist role. You'll move between frontend, backend and infrastructure, and you'll get to learn new parts of the stack as our needs change. If you like breadth, autonomy and building tools that make other people faster, this is the job.

### **What you might work on**

Projects change with what our research needs, but here are the kinds of things you could own:

* **Sandboxes for agents.** Design and run isolated environments where our models write and execute code, use tools and run experiments — safely, secure, reliably and at scale.
* **AI training infrastructure.** Build and improve our training systems (pretraining, midtraining, & posttraining): job scheduling, cluster management, training cookbooks, experiment tracking and the pipelines that move data and checkpoints around.
* **Research automation.** Build pipelines for automating the development of reinforcement learning environments, AI research, and AI self-alignment.
* **Apps that speed up researchers.** Build internal tools that help researchers plan, launch, monitor, compare and share experiments, so they spend less time on plumbing and more on research.
* **Coordination and work management.** Build the internal systems that help a fast-growing team track work, share results and stay in sync.

### **What you'll do**

* Own one or more internal systems end to end: design, execution and long-term maintenance.
* Find researcher problems before anyone files a ticket, and decide what's worth solving.
* Make sound technical decisions on your own, and explain the trade-offs clearly.
* Work across the stack, from user-facing interfaces to backend services and compute infrastructure.
* Keep what you build reliable, observable and easy for others to use.

### **You may be a good fit if you**

* Have shipped and maintained fullstack production software — frontend, backend and infrastructure — and are comfortable picking up whichever layer a problem needs.
* Have owned a project end to end, from scoping through design, build and ongoing operation.
* Have strong product sense: you can talk to users, work out what they really need and build something they'll use.
* Work well with a lot of autonomy. You set direction for your own work, make good technical calls without close oversight, and know when to ask for input.
* Have experience building internal tools, developer tooling, platforms or infrastructure for other engineers or researchers.
* Write clearly and communicate trade-offs to technical and non-technical colleagues.
* Have used AI agents not just as coding assistance, but as components in resilient infrastructure.

### **Bonus points**

* Experience with machine learning or large language model training, or the infrastructure behind them.
* Experience with high-performance computing, GPU clusters, job schedulers or container orchestration.
* Experience building sandboxed or isolated execution environments.
* Entrepreneurial experience — you've founded something, been an early engineer at a startup, or built a product from zero.

### **What we offer employees**

* Flexible PTO
* Monthly workspace and wellness allowances
* One conference a year fully covered
* 401(k) with automatic enrollment
* $10,000 Lifetime Fertility benefit
* Catered lunch daily, and breakfast twice a week in the SF office
* SF Moma museum membership

### **Logistics**

* **Location:** We currently expect all staff to work from our San Francisco office five days a week.
* **Visa sponsorship:** We sponsor visas. Not every role and candidate combination works out, but when we make an offer, we commit to a real effort, with support from immigration counsel we work with directly.

**Pantograph** is building general purpose intelligent robots that can safely and autonomously accomplish useful work in the real world. We believe the path to capable robots runs through general intelligence rather than narrow, robot-specific skills, and that there is an enormous amount of work worth doing in the physical world that would improve quality of life for people. As AI models make it easier to build software around our needs, we hope robots can empower people to shape the physical world.

Across research, hardware, and software, we focus on finding simple ideas that work, executing them extremely well, and scaling them up. We value clear thinking, careful execution, and systems we can understand, trust, and improve.

We're looking for a robotics ML engineer to design and build the systems that turn capable AI models into robots doing useful work. You'll bring a deep background in robotics and use it to decide how frontier models, learned policies, and classical controllers fit together. We see frontier models as an increasingly powerful foundation for general robot behavior, and want someone who can combine their capabilities with the methods robotics already does well.

The work includes connecting models to robot observations and actions, building the tools, skills, and controllers they rely on, and developing evaluations in simulation and on our fleet. You'll investigate when a frontier model should act directly, when it should coordinate faster learned policies or classical controllers, and when it should write its own tools or control code. You'll weigh the tradeoffs in capability, reliability, latency, safety, and how easily we can understand and supervise the system, with real deployments guiding your decisions.

You'll work closely with our research, robot software, and product teams, building a tight loop between experiments and experience on real hardware. We're looking for someone who combines excellent experimental judgment with a strong intuition for both robots and models, and enjoys building things to test their ideas. When something fails, you'll work out whether it calls for a better observation, a different tool, a change in orchestration, a better policy or controller, or a fix elsewhere in the system.

You might be a good fit if you:

* Have deep experience in robotics across areas such as control, perception, planning, and learned policies, and have made robots do useful work on real hardware
* Use simulation to develop and test systems, and understand where it diverges from reality
* Have designed and shipped robotic or AI systems that people use, with clear evidence of what made them better
* Are excellent at designing experiments and interpreting results: separating competing explanations, identifying confounders, and knowing what the evidence does and doesn't establish
* Have a strong intuition for how models behave: what they understand, what confuses them, and how their behavior changes with the tools, context, and feedback they receive
* Enjoy digging into failures and understanding how systems behave beyond aggregate metrics

Departmental Overview
  
  
Since its launch in 2013, BIDS has been dedicated to accelerating data-driven discovery by fostering an environment of open inquiry and cross-disciplinary collaboration. We have successfully broken down traditional academic silos, uniting domain experts from the life, physical, and social sciences, as well as the arts and humanities, with methodological leaders in computer science, statistics, and applied mathematics.
  
  
BIDS is expertly positioned as the central hub for advancing interdisciplinary data science research, academic training, and software development within the UC Berkeley College of Computing, Data Science, and Society. BIDS houses UC Berkeley's Open Source Program Office and champions open science, open source software, and open scholarship. We serve as a discipline-agnostic space to rally Berkeley's unique ecosystem, driving forward innovative collaborations that explore the profound impacts of Artificial Intelligence on both science and society.
  
  
UC Berkeley and UCSF have launched a joint program called the Bakar Computational Biomedicine Initiative to develop the frontier of AI and biomedicine, tremendously accelerating advances in clinical care. The new partnership brings together world-class faculty expertise in computing, AI, statistics, biology, and medicine, to speed discovery in everything from disease prevention, to early detection and new therapeutics in healthcare.
  
  
As part of this effort, at BIDS our team of open source research software engineers (OS-RSEs), product managers, and computational postdoctoral researchers will build the BioJupyter platform. Based on the widely adopted architecture of Project Jupyter and developed as part of the existing Jupyter ecosystem, with advancements and contributions to existing Jupyter components as well as the development of new tools, BioJupyter will bring next-generation features to facilitate collaboration in data-intensive, AI-powered biomedical research. * Develop prototypes, incorporate user feedback, and support user acceptance testing and adoption.
* Support and enhance vendor and proprietary systems used for lending data management, portfolio reporting, and servicing.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

* 3+ years of experience in technical roles within financial services.
* Relevant technical university degree.
* Professional experience with object-oriented programming using Python, Java, or C#.
* Experience with SQL and NoSQL databases and REST APIs, with a sound understanding of software design principles.
* Hands-on experience using AI tools to develop, test, and debug software, including reviewing and validating generated code.
* Experience integrating AI capabilities into applications and evaluating their outputs.
* Ability to clarify ambiguous business problems, ask effective questions, and translate findings into working software.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including explaining technical tradeoffs to nontechnical stakeholders.

**Preferred Qualifications and Experience**

* Experience with mortgages, commercial real estate, commercial loans, or other fixed income and credit products.
* Familiarity with loan financing structures and portfolio management, collateral management, or servicing workflows.
* Experience delivering workflow automation, process improvement, or digital transformation initiatives.
* Experience with financial data integration, reconciliation, or reporting.

  

**Base Salary Range**

$150,000-$200,000

The base salary range for this position is listed above. This position is also eligible for a discretionary annual bonus based on personal, team, and Firm performance. Compensation ranges are based on several factors including job function, level, and geographic location. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed here.

ATLAS SP is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.description:
Fifth Dimension is the most prominent AI company in real estate in the world, bringing the magic of AI automation to document-heavy industries . Our AI workspace helps leading investment managers, owners, and operators across the US, UK, and APAC automate complex workflows, extract insights from critical documents, and make faster, smarter decisions.

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Strategist to own delivery on our most important US accounts. You'll work in a pod with a forward deployed engineer, an account manager and our sales team, and you'll make the calls that decide whether a pilot becomes a firm-wide deployment: which workflow comes first, who needs to be in the room, what we build and what we don't. Customers will trust you because you understand their business. Our product team will listen to you because you've seen what works.

**What a week looks like**
--------------------------

**Monday.** Pod reviews across your three US accounts. One is on track. One has an MD asking for a bespoke dashboard. One has gone quiet: asset management hasn't logged in for ten days. You move that one to the top of the week.

**Tuesday.** On site with the quiet account. You sit with two asset managers through quarter-end and find the step that eats a week a month: reconciling operator reports against the rent roll. By the afternoon you've built a first version in the product, on their own documents, and they've told you what it gets wrong.

**Wednesday.** You move the FDE's week onto that workflow and off the dashboard. Then you write to the MD: why the dashboard can wait, what the team gets instead, and when.

**Thursday.** Two hours with our CTO and the FDEs. Three accounts have asked for some version of the same reconciliation. You bring the brief: what's common, what's one customer's preference, and what the template should be.

**Friday.** Three asset managers ran this week's reconciliation in 5D, and nobody opened the spreadsheet. You post the weekly update for each pod: what moved, what's stuck, what you decided. Then you sit in on a sales call with a prospect who has the same problem, to hear how they describe it.

This is a forward-deployed week at Fifth Dimension. You decide what we build for our most important customers, and you make sure they use it. What works in one account becomes product for all of them.

**About Us**
------------

Fifth Dimension builds AI software for the firms that invest in and manage real assets. We help people work with complex documents and business data, from leases and financial models to investment memos. We're a Series A company with offices in London, New York and Singapore.

Our values are Own It, Ship It and Don't Be Boring. We move quickly, challenge each other kindly and care about making something customers actually use.

**What This Role Is**
---------------------

* Owning delivery at a strategic level on a few of our US enterprise accounts after they sign: the use cases, the plan, the narrative and the decisions.
* Customer-facing for most of the week, often on site with investment, asset management and finance teams.
* Directing forward-deployed engineering time: deciding what our FDEs build and why, and changing course when a rollout stalls.
* The bridge to product: turning what works in one account into templates, skills and workflows that work in every account.
* AI-first. You build with AI yourself, and you can tell a customer exactly where it will and won't help.

**What This Role Is Not**
-------------------------

* A product manager role with a roadmap. You shape the product from the field; you don't own the backlog.
* An engineering role. You don't need to write production code; our FDEs do. You do need to build in the product and understand what's being built.
* Account management or customer success. Your pod has an account manager. You own the strategy, not the calendar.
* Sales. There's no quota. You'll sit in on sales calls to learn the market, not to close.

**The Challenge**
-----------------

A signed pilot is a bet, not a deployment. Real estate investment firms carry decades of process, documents in every format, and teams with good reason to be sceptical of AI. The first use case decides whether the rest of the firm follows.

Get it right and, six weeks in, the team uses it every day, the expansion conversation has started, and the workflow is a template every new customer starts from. Get it wrong and the pilot quietly expires.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

* Own the delivery plan for each of your accounts: the use cases, their order, the success criteria agreed up front, and the evidence that they were met.
* Decide where forward-deployed engineering time goes, and change it when a rollout stalls.
* Build alongside the team: workspaces, skills and templates in the product, prototyped with AI.
* Set the narrative: how the account understands 5D, from the analyst to the MD, including the hard conversations when expectations drift.
* Bring the field back: a short weekly update per account, and briefs that turn repeatable work into product.
* Become the domain expert in the room on the customer's workflow, their data and their language.

**About You**
-------------

You know real assets from the inside. You've worked in or alongside real estate investment, asset management or lending, and when you talk to a portfolio manager about a rent roll or an IC memo, they hear a peer.
